steps.what: Show the install window already approved for this room.
Direct the installation of operating systems, network or application software, or hardware.

tasks.design: The {CALENDAR} shows the install window already approved for the room. The systems engineer directs the installation of the operating system, the network or application software, or the hardware. The window does not install anything. A room with no approved window is left for the engineer to schedule.
tasks.previous_blocker: The install started from a verbal slot, and the room was still in use.
tasks.enabler_now: An approved window can be shown. Directing the installation still happens in the room.
tasks.still_hard: Stopping an install when the hardware in the room is not the hardware on the ticket stays with the engineer.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer directs the installation. The calendar slot is not the work.
tasks.altitude: Installation is still directed in the room. The approved window is only the time already agreed.

reach.task: Install a system inside a window the engineer has directed.
reach.learn: A calendar slot is not the installation.

evidence.claim: Showing an approved install window is a lookup of a time already agreed. It does not install the system.
Directing operating-system, software, or hardware installation stays in the room with the engineer.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A systems engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the design, and a draft is not the accepted system.
Fields: The room id and the window only if it is already approved. A blank window is not invented. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the systems engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the calendar entry before asking someone to read the same slot aloud.
unknowns: Whether hardware and software installs share one window record.
research_questions: Who may approve the window when the engineer is not the site owner?

already_counted.description: Directing the installation stays with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop windows whose installation has already finished.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still directs the installation of systems, software, or hardware in the room. Only showing a window that was already approved is removed. A room with no approved window saves none of that direction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List stored alerts for this system operation.
Monitor system operation to detect potential problems.

tasks.design: The {OPS_SYSTEM} lists alerts it has already stored. The detector's own run is not the engineer's time and is not counted. The systems engineer monitors the operation and decides which alerts are potential problems. A missing alert is not treated as a healthy system. The list does not make that judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: The engineer scrolled a raw log because the stored alert did not name the system.
tasks.enabler_now: Alerts already stored can be listed. Deciding which ones are problems still takes the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A quiet system with a failed detector still has to be noticed by a person.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer judges the alert. The detector's run is not the diagnosis.

ambition.what: Each stored alert is opened in the week it is raised, including alerts left in the queue.

tasks.altitude: Monitoring and the decision stay with the engineer. Listing stored alerts replaces scrolling the raw log, not the judgement.

reach.task: Work a problem the engineer has already judged real.
reach.learn: An alert id is not the diagnosis.

evidence.claim: Listing alerts already stored is a lookup. The detector that raised them is existing runtime and is not saved human labour.
Deciding which alert is a potential problem stays with the engineer. A missing alert is not proof that the system is well.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A systems engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the design, and a draft is not the accepted system.

Fields: The system id and alerts already stored against it. The screen does not invent an alert, and it does not treat a gap as zero. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the systems engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the stored alert list on the operations system before exporting the same rows again.
unknowns: Whether every monitored system writes alerts into the same list.
research_questions: Who judges an alert when the on-call engineer is not this role?

already_counted.description: Monitoring the operation and judging alerts stay with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop alerts whose system has been retired.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still monitors the operation and still decides which stored alerts are problems. Only listing alerts the detector has already stored is removed. The detector's run is not counted. A gap in the list saves nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show hardware and software components already recorded for this user.
Identify the components required to meet the user needs.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows hardware and software components already recorded against the user need. The systems engineer identifies which of them are required. The inventory is not that identification. A need with no recorded component is left blank, and the engineer names it after looking.
tasks.previous_blocker: The component list was last year's spreadsheet, and a retired server was still on it.
tasks.enabler_now: Recorded components can be shown. Identifying what the user needs still takes the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A need the record does not describe cannot be matched by the inventory alone.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer identifies what is required. The inventory is not the decision.
tasks.altitude: Identification stays with the engineer. The stored inventory only shows components already recorded.

reach.task: Confirm a data component the engineer has identified as required.
reach.learn: An inventory row is not the user's need.

evidence.claim: Showing recorded components is a lookup of the inventory. It does not identify what the user needs.
A blank need is not filled with a nearby component. The engineer identifies the requirement.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A systems engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the design, and a draft is not the accepted system.

Fields: The user-need id and components already recorded against it. Nothing is copied from a different need. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the systems engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the inventory record before building another component list.
unknowns: Whether hardware and software needs share one inventory record.
research_questions: Who confirms a component when the user cannot describe the need?

already_counted.description: Identifying the required components stays with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop component rows for needs that have been withdrawn.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still identifies the hardware or software components the user needs. Only showing components already recorded is removed. A need with nothing recorded saves none of that identification.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the maintenance window already agreed for this change.
Perform ongoing hardware and software maintenance, including installing or upgrading.

tasks.design: The {CALENDAR} shows the maintenance window already agreed. The systems engineer performs the hardware or software maintenance, including the install or the upgrade, on the equipment. The window does not do the work. A change with no window is not started from the screen.
tasks.previous_blocker: An upgrade started because the last one had worked, without a window for this change.
tasks.enabler_now: An agreed window can be shown. Installing and upgrading still happen on the equipment.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing that a unit still fails after the upgrade takes the engineer at the machine.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer installs and upgrades. The window is only the time already agreed.
tasks.altitude: Maintenance stays on the equipment with the engineer. The agreed window is not the install.

reach.task: Hand a machine back after the engineer has finished the upgrade.
reach.learn: A window on a calendar is not the maintenance.

evidence.claim: Showing an agreed maintenance window is a lookup of a time already set. It does not install or upgrade anything.
Hardware and software maintenance, including installing and upgrading, stays with the engineer on the equipment.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A systems engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the design, and a draft is not the accepted system.

Fields: The change id and the window only if it is already agreed. The screen does not open a window by itself. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the systems engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the calendar entry before walking to the rack.
unknowns: Whether hardware upgrades and software upgrades share one window type.
research_questions: Who is allowed to start maintenance when the agreed window has passed?

already_counted.description: Installing, upgrading, and the rest of the maintenance stay with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop windows whose maintenance has already been finished.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still performs the maintenance, including installing or upgrading, on the equipment. Only showing a window that was already agreed is removed. A change with no window saves none of that work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The systems engineer still directs installation, still judges alerts, and still installs the change. A stored window or a stored alert can be opened. The detector's own run is not this work.
reach: Network and computer systems administrators install and run the service, and this job learns the engineer directs that work rather than replacing it.
Computer network support specialists handle the call, and this job learns an alert id is not the diagnosis.
skills_to_grow: Direct an installation from the approved window, and stop when the room is not ready.
Judge a stored alert rather than treating the detector's run as the diagnosis.
Install and upgrade by hand, and do not copy last time's result forward.
role.ambitious_version: Installation, alert judgement, and maintenance stay with the engineer. Stored windows and stored alerts only show what was already recorded.
